subject: computer-science
summary: Computer Science is the tidiest of the four on desktop: stems are typed, code listings and tables are shown as crisp crops of the paper, and tick-list schemes (true/false, data types, wireframe elements) answer the question plainly. The main faults are in the text around them. Program output that the paper prints on separate lines is flattened into one run-on sentence, band-descriptor rubrics are printed as an unpunctuated string ('10 marks Correct response ... 8 marks Almost correct response ... 5 marks ...'), and alternative answers are joined with slashes and middle dots. Official scheme crops (worked answers, model code) are placed in the question column above the answer box rather than in the scheme, and one of them shows the answers to sibling parts. On a phone the code listings shrink badly: a 44-line program is squeezed into the column at about 5px per line.

issues.title: Expected program output flattened into the sentence
issues.detail: Card 3's question ends '...the output may now look as follows: ******************** Times Table program ******************** Multiplications of 7 0 7 14 21 28 35 42 49 56 63', one run-on line where the paper shows a multi-line console output. Card 7 ends 'Score Password ----- -------- 1 sun 6 Sun 11 Sunshine 0 12345 11 Moonlight', a two-column table collapsed to a string with stray dash runs. Both are in the large serif question type, so the mess is prominent.
issues.suggested_fix: Render sample output in a monospace block with its original line breaks (or crop it from the paper like the code listing).

issues.title: Band-descriptor rubric printed as a run-on string
issues.detail: Level-of-response schemes show the rubric as one unpunctuated grey paragraph under the bold answer: card 3 '(ii) 10 marks (B-10 scale) 10 marks Correct response Correct insertion of row of asterisks in both locations 8 marks Almost correct response Correct implementation using solution above or similar but with minor syntax or semantic error 5 marks Response with some merit Any other reasonable attempt.'; card 7 the same pattern for a B-5 scale; cards 1, 2, 5, 6, 10 'Very good description - clear understanding demonstrated 3 marks Fair description - limited understanding 2 marks'. The mark buttons (0 5 8 10) sit below with no labels, so the student has to parse the paragraph to learn what 8 means. 'B-10 scale' is examiner jargon.
issues.suggested_fix: Lay the bands out as rows ('10 — correct: asterisks in both places', '8 — almost correct: minor syntax error', '5 — some merit') and make each row the tappable score, replacing the bare number buttons.

issues.title: Scheme crops sit in the question column and can show other parts' answers
issues.detail: After reveal, the official answer crop appears under the question, above 'Open original paper' and the empty answer box, with no 'answer' heading: card 2 (the (i)/(ii) worked answers), card 3 (model program), card 7 (two solution lines), card 9 (completed test plan), card 10 (hex conversion). On the phone the tick list is a screen further down. Card 3's model program is the solution to the whole of Q16(a): it carries tags #(i) to #(vi), so it gives away the input, if/else and range(13) answers to sibling parts and its range and print lines no longer match the program in the question. Card 7's crop (lines 75-76) is pale grey on grey and about 5px high on the phone.
issues.suggested_fix: Move the crop into the scheme panel under 'Official solution'. For multi-part solutions crop or highlight only the lines for this part (card 3: lines 3-5), or type the answer lines as a code block.

issues.title: Code listings too small on a phone
issues.detail: Card 7's 44-line program is fitted to the 330px column, giving roughly 5px line height and unreadable identifiers; card 4's 11-line listing is about 9px per line with pale red numbers; card 3's is borderline. Card 8's true/false statements and card 9's two tables are also noticeably smaller than body text on the phone. All are fine on desktop, and Enlarge exists, but the question cannot be read in place.
issues.suggested_fix: Render code as real monospace text in a horizontally scrollable block, or show only the lines the part refers to (card 7 needs lines 40-44) with the full listing behind Enlarge.

issues.title: Questions missing a piece or with muddled structure
issues.detail: Card 4 asks 'State the purpose of each of the operators listed below.' but no operators are listed; the student only learns they are % and // from the scheme. Card 2 lists (a), (b), (i), (ii) at one indent level, so (i) and (ii) do not read as children of (b). Card 5's stem runs the article headline into its first sentence ('...following Apple and Google's model Ireland is the latest European country...'). Card 7's stem keeps list hyphens inline ('two main differences: - The code ... - Instead of ...'), and card 4's stem runs 'Step 1: ... Step 2: ... Step 3: ... Step 4:' together. Card 12 puts the table crop above the instruction with no stem.
issues.suggested_fix: Add the operator list ('% and //') to card 4; indent sub-parts under their parent; set headlines, bullet lists and numbered steps on their own lines.

issues.title: Alternatives joined by slashes and dots; table answers flattened
issues.detail: Card 1's scheme reads 'Dog owners / general public / customers — end-users' then 'K9-Kennels / John and Mary and their employees — client / project sponsor Users of the system · Software company including any relevant job title e.g. project manager / analyst / designer / programmer / tester etc. — Any relevant description', three stakeholder/role pairs mashed into one paragraph with a stray 'Users of the system'. Card 5 strings seven testing types with ' · '. Card 9's answers lose their columns ('A2 1.2 Water served, no change given', 'C1 <2 Error – not enough money inserted') and do not show which cell was the blank. Card 12 has no separator between value and type ('Ciara String/str', '255 int/integer'). Card 10(b) joins the two steps with a bullet character and drops the first method shown in the crop.
issues.suggested_fix: One row per acceptable answer ('Stakeholder: dog owners / customers — Role: end-users'); for table answers show 'Code entered: A2', 'Money inserted: less than 2', 'Expected result: Error...' or 'Ciara → String (str)'.

good_examples.why: Typed stem, clean crop of the true/false grid, four full-sentence answers each ending in True/False with 1 mark.
Clear wireframe question and four short 1-mark criteria; nothing extraneous.
Table crop is large and legible on both devices and the six answers line up with it row for row.
